title: Sabrina Carpenter's songwriter Amy Allen writes the pop music stuck in your head
locator: body paragraphs numbered from the NEW YORK lead (para 1)
notes: The same AP text was also fetched as republished by the Boston Globe on 2024-12-20 (https://www.bostonglobe.com/2024/12/20/arts/amy-allen-interview-grammys-sabrina-carpenter). The account of how Espresso was written comes from Julian Bunetta (para 11), not Allen. AP places the session in a Paris studio, while Wikipedia (AA-S17) says Flow Studios, Chailland, France. Allen gives no account of how the song was written.

title: Meet the Grammy-winning Maine songwriter behind big pop hits like 'Espresso'
notes: Allen says sessions vary: some artists arrive with lyrics or a musical idea, some with nothing, some as a Zoom call about feelings (paras 12-14). She says you can't tell whether there is writing chemistry until you actually write together (para 15). The 'ironic, silly, sexy' description of the Carpenter songs is the author's, not Allen's (para 43).

title: Amy Allen Reflects on Becoming 'Really Close' with Sabrina Carpenter While Making 'Man's Best Friend' (Exclusive)
locator: answers A3-A5, A9 numbered by me
notes: Allen says that when they needed a second verse on Man's Best Friend they often took long walks and talked until ideas came (A4a). Asked about Manchild specifically, she answered about the whole album and gave no account of writing that song. No date or byline was visible.
